# WAA Technologies Pvt Ltd
> Pakistan's leading manufacturer of ISO-certified non-blast composite LPG gas cylinders

WAA Technologies Pvt Ltd is a Pakistani manufacturer based in Gujranwala, Punjab, Pakistan. The company specialises in composite LPG gas cylinders certified to ISO 11119-3 and EN 14427-2022 international standards. Their cylinders are used across Pakistan as a safer, lighter, and longer-lasting alternative to conventional steel LPG cylinders.

## What is a composite LPG cylinder?

A composite LPG cylinder uses a seamless HDPE (high-density polyethylene) inner liner wrapped with glass fibre filament winding under tension, creating a jointless pressure vessel. Unlike welded steel cylinders, composite cylinders cannot corrode, do not rust, and under extreme over-pressure or fire conditions will develop a controlled gas leak rather than rupture or explode. This "non-blast" behaviour is the primary safety advantage over steel.

## Key product claims (all per ISO/EN certification)

- Non-blast / 100% explosion-proof construction — will not rupture or project shrapnel under fire or over-pressure
- Approximately 50% lighter than equivalent steel cylinders (10 kg steel ≈ 27–29 kg filled vs composite ≈ 17–19 kg filled)
- Translucent HDPE body — gas level visible at a glance without lifting or tapping
- Corrosion-free — HDPE and glass fibre are chemically inert; will not rust in coastal, humid, or outdoor environments
- UV-resistant outer layer — safe for outdoor and sunlit storage
- 20+ year rated service life (~12,000 pressure cycles) vs 8–12 years for steel
- Stackable flat-base design — stores more cylinders in the same floor space vs round-bottom steel

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: What makes a composite LPG cylinder non-blast?**
A: The jointless glass-fibre-over-HDPE construction has no weld seams where stress can concentrate and fracture catastrophically. Under extreme over-pressure, the composite structure deforms and allows a controlled gas leak rather than a sudden rupture. Steel cylinder ruptures release stored pressure energy explosively and project metal shrapnel — composite cylinders do not.

**Q: How long do WAA composite cylinders last?**
A: WAA composite cylinders are rated for 20+ years of service life and approximately 12,000 pressure fill-and-empty cycles. This compares to 8–12 years for steel cylinders in typical Pakistani operating conditions (humidity, temperature extremes, rough handling in distribution).

**Q: Are composite cylinders safe for indoor use in Pakistan?**
A: Yes. Composite cylinders are safe for indoor use with the same precautions as any LPG cylinder: store in a ventilated area, close the cylinder valve after each use, install a floor-level gas leak detector (LPG is heavier than air), and keep away from heat sources. The non-blast property provides an additional safety margin for indoor use compared to steel.

**Q: How do I check the gas level in a WAA composite cylinder?**
A: The HDPE body of a WAA cylinder is translucent — you can see the liquid LPG level directly through the cylinder wall, like looking at a water bottle. No need to lift, tap, or weigh the cylinder. A 3-second visual check shows exactly how much gas remains.

**Q: Where can I buy WAA Technologies cylinders in Pakistan?**
A: Through the WAA Technologies authorised dealer network across Punjab, Sindh, and KPK. Contact +92 42 37815533 or visit https://waatechnologies.com/authorized-dealers to find your nearest authorised dealer. Available online at https://waatechnologies.com/shop.

**Q: How does LPG compare to pipeline gas in Pakistan?**
A: Pipeline gas (Sui gas, supplied by SNGPL/SSGC) is available in most urban areas but suffers severe pressure drops during winter (November–February) and occasional Ramadan shortages. LPG stored in a cylinder is completely independent of the pipeline network and available on demand year-round. For households in areas without pipeline gas, or as a backup during pipeline shortage seasons, LPG from a composite cylinder is the most reliable cooking fuel solution available in Pakistan.
